figures.name: leaves_parts_rebuilt

figures.name: leaves_parts_deferred
figures.basis: predicted: the rebuild covers every part of a quiescent ci tenant in one run

figures.name: leaves_parts_erasure_gated
figures.basis: predicted: nothing is erased on a fresh ci tenant

figures.name: leaves_parts_over_cap
figures.basis: predicted: no ci part holds more entries than the rebuild's per-part cap

figures.name: leaves_uncovered_entries
figures.basis: predicted: every entry of a rebuilt ci part is covered by its leaves

figures.name: unrouted_label_value_leaf_parts
figures.basis: predicted: no fold before stage1-leaves runs with --fold-metrics-label-index, so the unrouted pass reads a snapshot without label_value leaves (run.sh refuses the pass otherwise)

figures.name: routed_label_value_leaf_parts
figures.basis: predicted: the routed pass reads the snapshot stage1-leaves published, with at least one part carrying a label_value leaf

figures.name: entries_compared
figures.basis: predicted: both steady passes return a result_hash for at least one corpus entry

figures.name: entries_differing
figures.basis: predicted: routing prunes objects, never results, so every entry's unrouted and routed hashes are equal

figures.name: entries_multi_hash
figures.basis: predicted: every pass repeats its own answer, so no entry carries two or more result_hash values within a pass; an entry whose two passes carry the same set of several hashes is non-determinism inside a pass, not a routing difference

figures.name: entries_without_hash
figures.basis: predicted: every corpus entry answers (ok or incorrect, both carrying a result_hash) in both passes on ci

figures.name: statements_status_differing
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 9): routing changes which objects are opened, never the oracle's verdict, so each entry's set of record statuses is the same in the unrouted and routed passes; an entry known to be incorrect stays incorrect in both

figures.name: unrouted_records_status_unexpected
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 9): every unrouted record's status is ok or incorrect on ci; partial, timeout, error, unsupported_construct, refused or a failure string counts here

figures.name: routed_records_status_unexpected
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 9): every routed record's status is ok or incorrect on ci; partial, timeout, error, unsupported_construct, refused or a failure string counts here

figures.name: unrouted_records_answered_null_hash
figures.basis: predicted: every unrouted record whose status is ok or incorrect carries a result_hash (records with another status are counted by records_status_unexpected instead)

figures.name: routed_records_answered_null_hash
figures.basis: predicted: every routed record whose status is ok or incorrect carries a result_hash (records with another status are counted by records_status_unexpected instead)

figures.name: unrouted_records_label_index_null
figures.basis: predicted: every unrouted record carries a segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex figure

figures.name: routed_records_label_index_null
figures.basis: predicted: every routed record carries a segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex figure

figures.name: unrouted_records_pruned_by_label_index
figures.basis: predicted: with no label_value leaf in the snapshot, no unrouted record prunes an object through the label index

figures.name: unrouted_cold_records
figures.basis: predicted: no corpus entry of class long_range or mb_full_range_avg_over_time is declared for ci, so stage1.unrouted_cold says not applicable and its count is 0 of 0; on a profile that selects cold entries the band is at least entries x 5 repetitions, and a cold stamp that failed or is absent leaves no count, which fails as missing

figures.name: unrouted_cold_records_short
figures.basis: predicted: every selected cold entry x repetition has a record with a ravel_cost (0 selected on ci)

figures.name: routed_cold_records
figures.basis: predicted: no corpus entry of class long_range or mb_full_range_avg_over_time is declared for ci, so stage1.routed_cold says not applicable and its count is 0 of 0; on a profile that selects cold entries the band is at least entries x 5 repetitions, and a cold stamp that failed or is absent leaves no count, which fails as missing

figures.name: routed_cold_records_short
figures.basis: predicted: every selected cold entry x repetition has a record with a ravel_cost (0 selected on ci)

figures.name: holders_objects_above_watermark
figures.basis: predicted: the fold step ran with --writers-stopped after the last write, so every listed object's ingest hour is at or below the folded watermark

figures.name: holders_window_mismatches
figures.basis: predicted: every unrouted record's segmentsFetched equals its statement's unrouted_fetched_expected, the resolved set plus token_only_fetched: the resolved set is named_in_window (the objects in the window holding a series of the statement's one metric, since the unrouted resolve prunes by that name's postings) when every selector names one metric and segments_in_window (every object in the window) when they name different metrics; token_only_fetched is the listed L0 objects outside that set named by a min_commit_token the query lane passed (one per shard), which the resolve adds whatever their metrics and event time. Run 42495422937 gave 1 here with the token objects left out: mb_absent_selective_labels expected 0 and fetched its 4 shards' token objects

figures.name: holders_window_unchecked
figures.basis: predicted: every counted statement has unrouted records, each with a whole-number segmentsFetched, and a whole-number unrouted_fetched_expected (every min_commit_token the query lane passed names a listed object)

figures.name: holders_routed_prune_mismatches
figures.basis: predicted: for each route_bound statement, every routed record's segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex equals expected_routed_prunes, the resolved set (named_in_window for one metric, segments_in_window for several) less value_holders, the objects of that set whose LABEL_DICT holds, for at least one selector, its metric name and every label="value" value; the router keeps the rest, and objects only a min_commit_token adds are never routed. Run 42495422937 would give 0: every ci object's LABEL_DICT holds every probed value, so value_holders equals named_in_window and the expected and observed prunes are both 0. This replaces routed_records_pruned_by_label_index at least 1, which that run failed with 0 because nothing on ci can be pruned

figures.name: holders_routed_prune_unchecked
figures.basis: predicted: every route_bound statement has routed records, each with a whole-number segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex, and a whole-number expected_routed_prunes

figures.name: holders_routed_leaf_unread
figures.basis: predicted: every routed record of a route_bound statement whose resolved set holds an object shows a leaf read in its keyIndex phase (s3GetRequests or cacheHits above 0), so a prune count of 0 means the router read the leaves and kept every object, not that it never ran; a statement whose resolved set is empty is not counted (its snapshot holds only token objects, which carry no leaf). Run 42495422937 would give 0: its routed keyIndex phases showed cacheHits of 10 and 4 with no GET

figures.name: route_values_records
figures.basis: predicted: every corpus selector carries a __name__ equality and the routed snapshot carries label_value leaves, so the route runs and at least one routed record lists its passes in labelIndexValues; 0 means no per-value figure below was measured

figures.name: route_values_unreadable
figures.basis: predicted: every routed record's labelIndexValues element carries labels and whole-number leafGetRequests, leafCacheHits, partsCovered, partsBeyondCeiling and segmentsPrunedAlone, as the server renders them

figures.name: route_values_leaf_gets_over_bound
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 per-value routing amendment): a statement with n distinct values issues at most n passes' leaf GETs, so no routed record's summed leafGetRequests exceeds (1 + n) x the parts its passes cover

figures.name: route_values_parts_beyond_ceiling
figures.basis: predicted: a ci snapshot holds few enough parts that no pass reaches the router's leaf GET or part ceiling, so no pass leaves a part unprobed (partsBeyondCeiling summed over every routed record's passes)

figures.name: holders_selective_job_rate_sum
figures.basis: predicted: job="metricsbench-api" series are written on every ci run, so at least one data object holds a series matching the statement's one selector in full (holders is a series-level index's bound; the router's is value_holders, checked through holders_routed_prune_mismatches)

figures.name: control_statements_more_gets
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 12): the unrouted pass runs the main image with the leaf router idle (no label_value leaf in the snapshot), so no statement's median GETs per record exceed the control image's on the same snapshot

figures.name: control_statements_more_bytes
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 12): as control_statements_more_gets, for the median wire bytes per record summed over phases

figures.name: control_statements_unchecked
figures.basis: predicted: every corpus entry has an answered record carrying s3GetRequests and s3GetWireBytes in every phase in both passes, so no statement goes uncompared

figures.name: control_statements_slower
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 12, no statement over 5 % slower outside the lane's noise): no statement whose unrouted median latency_ms exceeds the control's by more than 5 % of the control's and by more than the larger of the two passes' spreads (max minus min of its latency_ms), the run's measure of the lane's noise; the ids are statements_slower

figures.name: extra_hour_tail_objects
figures.basis: predicted: the extra hour lands in an ingest hour above the routed watermark, so the leaf-on fold folds at least one new data object; 0 means the leaf ratio below measured nothing

figures.name: extra_hour_start_mismatches
figures.basis: predicted: the leaf-off fold starts from the leafless HEAD and the leaf-on fold from the routed HEAD, two different HEADs, so only their previous_watermark_hour is compared, and both report the same one

figures.name: extra_hour_leaf_bytes_ratio
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 7, leaf bytes at most 1 % of part data bytes): the leaf bytes the leaf-on fold writes stay within 1% of the data object bytes of the hours its tail parts span (leaf_bytes_denominator), the fold's own per-part leaf cap; a tail part is a part the leaf-on fold's HEAD carries and the routed HEAD it started from does not (key and blake3), a re-encoded part over older hours included (repartitioned_parts)

figures.name: extra_hour_tail_parts
figures.basis: predicted: the leaf-on fold publishes at least one part, by key and blake3, that the routed HEAD does not carry; 0 means extra_hour_uncovered_tail_parts and the leaf ratio's denominator checked no part

figures.name: extra_hour_uncovered_tail_parts
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 7): every tail part (a part the leaf-on fold's HEAD carries and the routed HEAD does not, by key and blake3) carries label_value leaves with no uncovered entry

figures.name: extra_hour_wall_ratio_on_off
figures.basis: predicted, loose, ci only: the leaf-on fold's wall time from the routed HEAD over the leaf-off fold's from the leafless HEAD, each folding the same new hour; building one hour's leaves costs a ranged GET per data object and a PUT per leaf, which should not take ten times a fold that writes none. This is not ADR-3694 row 7's target (switch on within 10 % of off, 1.10; miss over 20 %, 1.20), which a ci fold of a few objects, timed in milliseconds, cannot resolve

figures.name: l1_objects
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 6, #3818): compact-tenant compacts at least one sealed hour, so the folded snapshot lists at least one L1 object

figures.name: l1_entries_differing
figures.basis: predicted: compaction rewrites objects, never results, and the extra hour lies after every query window, so every entry's routed and L1 hashes are equal

figures.name: l1_entries_compared
figures.basis: predicted: both passes return a result_hash for at least one corpus entry

figures.name: l1_records_status_unexpected
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 6, #3818): every L1 record's status is ok or incorrect, so no refusal of any kind, fetch memory exhausted included, and no error

figures.name: erasure_reference_prune_mismatch
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): the reference pass routes as the routed pass does, so on every entry both passes answered with a result_hash each record prunes as many segments by label index in both (label_index_prune_basis); the pending pass's no-prune is then read against a reference whose routing is the routed pass's, whatever its prune count

figures.name: erasure_subject_entries_differing
figures.basis: predicted: metricsbench-instance-0 series are written on every ci run, so excluding them changes at least one entry's answer against the routed pass; otherwise the pending comparison cannot show the subject hidden

figures.name: erasure_pending_status_unexpected
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): every pending record's status is ok or incorrect, so no statement is refused or errors while the erasure is pending

figures.name: erasure_pending_entries_without_hash
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): every corpus entry carries a result_hash in both the reference and the pending pass, so the equality check covers every entry

figures.name: erasure_pending_label_index_null
figures.basis: predicted: every pending record carries a whole segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex, so erasure_pending_pruned_by_label_index counts over every record rather than passing on a missing figure

figures.name: erasure_pending_pruned_by_label_index
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): while an erasure is pending the router prunes nothing, so no pending record has a segmentsPrunedByLabelIndex above 0

figures.name: erasure_pending_entries_differing
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): a pending erasure hides its subject at query time, so each pending entry answers as the reference pass, the routed corpus with every selector excluding instance="metricsbench-instance-0"

figures.name: erasure_pending_entries_compared
figures.basis: predicted: both passes return a result_hash for at least one corpus entry

figures.name: erasure_erased_hours
figures.basis: predicted: metricsbench-instance-0 series are written on every ci run, so the rewrite replaces the data objects of at least one ingest hour; an erased hour is an ingest_hour_bucket holding a catalog list --json key before the erasure that is not listed after its fold, since a rewrite output is a new content-keyed L1 key in the same hour (crates/ravel-maintain/src/erasure_rewrite.rs build_rewrite_part, keys::l1_part_key) that supersedes its inputs. A compaction the maintain container ran in the same window also reads as an erased hour

figures.name: erasure_carried_over_erased_hours
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): after the rewrite and a fold, no pre-erasure part whose lo..=hi range holds an erased hour is still in the catalog with the same key and blake3; each one left is listed in carried_over_parts

figures.name: erasure_stale_leaves
figures.basis: predicted (ADR-3694 row 8): after the rewrite and a fold, no part in the post-fold inspect references a key-index leaf that a pre-erasure part over an erased hour (an overlapping part) referenced
